convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom() to call multiple custom indicators (XCCI_Histogram_Vol, ColorAcceleration_Histogram, ColorXXD_Histogram) which are external .mqh-based or .ex5 compiled indicators. The custom indicator logic is not accessible from built-in MT5 indicators, requiring manual replication of the indicator algorithms for Python conversion.

other_exits: Opposite signal from XCCI_Histogram_Vol closes existing position before opening new one in the opposite direction

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MMType parameter selects between fixed lots (negative values) and deposit fraction (positive values as percentage of free margin)

custom_logic_notes: Three-custom-indicator consensus system: all three histogram indicators must agree on direction (all bullish for long, all bearish for short). The XCCI_Histogram_Vol indicator is a CCI derivative with volume weighting and JMA smoothing. ColorAcceleration_Histogram is based on Bill Williams' Acceleration/Deceleration oscillator with color-coded histogram. ColorXXD_Histogram is a DeMarker oscillator variant with similar coloring. The EA checks previous bar values (bar index 1) for signal confirmation, not current bar. On opposite signal, the existing position is closed first then a new position is opened. Trailing stop is optional (default 0 = disabled). Money management has two modes: fixed lots when MMType value is negative, or deposit fraction when positive.
python_conversion_notes: Three custom indicators must be reverse-engineered or reimplemented in Python. XCCI_Histogram_Vol requires CCI calculation with volume weighting and JMA/Ehlers smoothing. ColorAcceleration_Histogram requires Bill Williams AO/AC oscillator logic with trend coloring. ColorXXD_Histogram requires DeMarker oscillator with similar coloring. The consensus (AND) logic across all three is straightforward once indicators are available. Digit adjustment logic must be handled for pip-to-point conversion. The signal checks previous completed bar (shift=1), not current bar. Position management is simple: one position at a time, close-opposite-then-open pattern.
